prompt: Analyze the LeadSuccess.csv dataset: calculate the number of leads created per month, identify the month with the highest lead volume, and compute the month-over-month growth rate. Present results as a table with columns: Month, Lead Count, Growth Rate (%).
expectedAnswer: The analysis should show monthly lead counts derived from the Created Date column, identify the peak month, and calculate percentage growth between consecutive months. Exact values depend on the dataset but the methodology must use date parsing and aggregation.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Monthly counts are accurate, growth rates are calculated correctly as percentage change

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: All months in the dataset are covered, peak month identified, growth rates for all consecutive months

criteria.name: Formatting
criteria.description: Clean table format with Month, Lead Count, Growth Rate columns

criteria.name: Methodology
criteria.description: Proper date parsing, chronological ordering, correct percentage calculation formula

prompt: Analyze the LeadSuccess.csv dataset for outliers: identify leads with Annual Revenue values more than 2 standard deviations from the mean within their sector. For each outlier, report the Company, Sector, Annual Revenue, sector mean, sector std dev, and z-score. Also report which sectors have the most outliers.
expectedAnswer: The analysis should compute per-sector mean and standard deviation of Annual Revenue, identify rows where |z-score| > 2, and rank sectors by outlier count. The methodology must handle missing values and use correct statistical formulas.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Statistical calculations (mean, std dev, z-score) are correct per sector

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: All outliers identified, per-outlier details provided, sector ranking included

criteria.name: Formatting
criteria.description: Clear table with Company, Sector, Revenue, Mean, StdDev, Z-Score columns

criteria.name: Methodology
criteria.description: Proper handling of missing values, correct z-score formula, per-sector grouping

prompt: Analyze the LeadSuccess.csv dataset for correlations: compute the relationship between Annual Revenue and Number of Employees across all leads. Calculate the Pearson correlation coefficient, determine if larger companies (by revenue) tend to have more employees, and identify the top 5 companies that deviate most from the trend (highest residuals). Also analyze whether Lead Source correlates with Annual Revenue by computing mean revenue per source.
expectedAnswer: The analysis should compute Pearson r between Annual Revenue and Number of Employees, report the correlation strength, identify the 5 highest-residual companies, and rank Lead Sources by mean Annual Revenue. Methodology must handle missing values and use correct correlation formula.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Pearson correlation coefficient is correctly computed, residuals correctly identified, mean revenues per source accurate

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: Both analyses (revenue-employees correlation + source-revenue breakdown) completed with all requested details

criteria.name: Formatting
criteria.description: Clear presentation with correlation value, interpretation, residual table, and source ranking table

criteria.name: Methodology
criteria.description: Proper Pearson formula, correct residual calculation from linear fit, appropriate handling of missing data
